set.body:
Objective:
Extend Frame physical execution only after the independent local engine and first adapters establish stable semantics and real workload evidence.

Candidate scope:
- Bounded-memory spill for blocking local sort, hash aggregation, and hash join.
- External sort and partitioned aggregation/join strategies.
- Asynchronous or effect-adapted batch pulling without changing the pure logical plan.
- Plan segmentation where a fully supported subplan may run in DuckDB, an explicitly local or Gale-backed transform runs in its adapter, and remaining relational work returns to Frame.
- Statistics-driven physical choices, common-subexpression handling, dictionary-aware strategies, and adaptive batch sizing.
- A Spark translator is created only after a named consumer demonstrates demand and a conformance subset; Spark never shapes Frame core.

Non-negotiable rules:
- Segmentation boundaries are explicit in explain output and carry Arrow ownership/copy receipts.
- No backend fallback or repartitioning is silent.
- Every physical optimization preserves the semantic constitution or rejects the requested mode.
- Spill files are scoped, recoverable, and cleaned on success, failure, cancellation, and process-restart recovery according to a documented policy.
- Frame core remains scheduler-, effect-, Spark-, DuckDB-, Gale-, and filesystem-implementation-neutral.

Acceptance:
- Measured workloads establish which operations need spill, segmentation, or adaptive planning.
- Differential and metamorphic tests compare each advanced route to the local reference on declared supported inputs.
- Peak-memory receipts demonstrate bounded behavior for spill-capable operations.
- Interrupted and failed executions do not expose partial final results or orphan untracked spill state.
- JVM-only advanced adapters do not weaken Scala.js core or local-engine guarantees.
set.title: Frame execution: spill, segmented backends, async pulls, and evidence-driven physical planning
